look_here_first: LOOK AT A REAL LEAF CLOSE-UP FIRST: both leaf faces and outer phyllaries are densely coated in separate, long, SILVERY, SOFT HAIRS lying near-parallel to the surface (sericeous hairs). At hand-lens scale, follow individual white hairs across the green blade; a silvery glare alone is not evidence. Then inspect the SILKY outer phyllaries on a closed flower bud, the often wiry/low perennial shoots and a thickened woody/cormoid rootstock. Purple rays and yellow-purple center are secondary; true S. oblongifolium has rough shorter hairs, narrow phyllaries and upper-stem glandular hairs rather than this even silky leaf coat. Beware Texas S. pratense, a look-alike with much LESS dense silky hair and wider ovate phyllaries, not yet a canonical learner species.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Look for individual long soft appressed white/silver hairs along BOTH sides of the leaf blade; a close-up is now licensed and included in images[].

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Silky-haired outer involucral bracts (phyllaries) around mature closed flower buds and beneath open heads; photo of bud and flower now included.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Low-wiry clumping perennial with short thickened rootstock/cormoid crown; old basal leaves may wither by flowering; do not expect only one specific height.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves mainly alternate and sessile to nearly so; often narrow oblong/elliptic, entire, increasingly shorter toward the branch tips.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Several purple-to-lavender rays with disk heads aging toward dull reddish-purple; COLOR is NOT decisive.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Against S. oblongifolium: deeply silver-sericeous foliage versus rougher green leaves with short hairs/glands; flower color overlaps.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Against S. pratense: similar Texan silver-ish aster, but with LESS dense hair on leaves and distinctly broader ovate phyllaries; check photo-vouchered plant.

lookalikes.differences: Use the individual long appressed silky hairs on both leaf surfaces plus densely sericeous involucral bracts, and confirm a thickened wiry perennial base. Against aromatic S. oblongifolium look for rough or glandular upper structures rather than even long silky hairs; S. pratense can still look slightly silky but has sparser leaf hairs and broader ovate phyllaries (taxonomic specialist Semple 2025).
